property_summary: After calling Put(uint _unlockTime) with any caller and any payable value, the contract's stored unlockTime for that caller is always >= block.timestamp (reference enforces max(block.timestamp,_unlockTime)); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs, violating this rule.

For any caller and any payable amount, after Put(_unlockTime) completes the stored unlockTime for that caller is never less than the current block.timestamp (reference uses max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)); the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can make it less than block.timestamp for some _unlockTime inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored unlockTime for that caller is never less than the block.timestamp observed immediately after the call (reference enforces unlockTime = max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that assigns unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it < block.timestamp for some inputs).

For any caller and any payable value, calling Put(_unlockTime) results in the contract's stored unlockTime for that caller being >= the block.timestamp observed at the start of the Put call; the mutant that assigns acc.unlockTime = _unlockTime can set it below the call's start timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime values, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any payable amount, after calling Put(_unlockTime) where _unlockTime >= block.timestamp the stored unlockTime for that caller equals _unlockTime (reference enforces max but when _unlockTime is already >= block.timestamp both behave the same); the mutant breaks this rule only when _unlockTime < block.timestamp but we restrict inputs so _unlockTime >= block.timestamp — this rule holds for the reference for all admissible inputs and the mutant can still be distinguished by allowing _unlockTime < block.timestamp in other runs, so keeping admissible domain ensures the reference always satisfies it.

For any caller and any deposited amount/unlockTime, after Put the account's unlockTime is at least the block.timestamp provided to Put (i.e. acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp at call return); the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime to block.timestamp can violate intended behavior when caller passes a larger _unlockTime (making unlockTime be less than the intended future unlock time).

For any caller and any provided _unlockTime, after Put completes the stored unlockTime for that caller is >= the block.timestamp at call time and equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that always sets unlockTime to block.timestamp can produce a stored unlockTime < provided _unlockTime when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller, calling Put with a future _unlockTime should set Acc[caller].unlockTime to at least that _unlockTime (i.e., stored unlockTime >= provided _unlockTime); the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can make the stored unlockTime < provided future _unlockTime.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, calling Put should set Acc[caller].unlockTime to be at least the maximum of the previous stored unlockTime and the provided _unlockTime (i.e., it should never decrease below the prior unlockTime or below the provided _unlockTime when that provided value is later); the mutant that always sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can decrease the stored unlockTime compared to the previous value when caller supplies a smaller _unlockTime and block.timestamp is less than the previous unlockTime.

For any caller and any inputs, calling Put(...) never decreases that caller's stored unlockTime below its previous value (i.e., Acc[caller].unlockTime after Put >= previous Acc[caller].unlockTime); the mutant that unconditionally sets unlockTime = block.timestamp can reduce unlockTime when block.timestamp is less than the prior stored unlockTime.

After calling Put(...) the holder's unlockTime in the reference is set to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) (never decreases below block.timestamp), whereas the mutant leaves unlockTime unchanged — violating this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and deposit amount, after Put(...) completes the holder's unlockTime is at least the current block.timestamp and is equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave unlockTime < block.timestamp or not reflect max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) for some inputs.

After any caller invokes Put(_unlockTime) with any deposit amount, the holder's unlockTime is set to at least the current block.timestamp and equals max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave unlockTime lower than block.timestamp or not equal to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp) for some inputs.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) (possibly with value), the holder's unlockTime is never decreased below its previous value and is at least block.timestamp (i.e., unlockTime_new >= max(unlockTime_old, block.timestamp)); the mutant that omits updating unlockTime can leave unlockTime unchanged and thus violate that rule when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and deposit amount, after Put(...) completes the holder's unlockTime equals either its previous value or max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp); the correct contract always sets unlockTime to at least block.timestamp (specifically max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp)), while the mutant that removes the update can leave unlockTime unchanged even when it should become >= block.timestamp — so we assert that if the holder's balance increased then unlockTime >= block.timestamp (a rule the mutant can violate).

After calling Put(u) from any sender with any msg.value, the contract sets the sender's stored unlockTime to max(u, block.timestamp); the mutant flips the choice and thus can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some inputs.

For any caller and any _unlockTime, after Put the stored unlockTime is >= block.timestamp (the contract never sets a past unlockTime); the mutant flips the ternary and can set unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this property.

For any caller and any _unlockTime and msg.value, after Put completes the stored unlockTime is either equal to the supplied _unlockTime when it is in the future or else equal to the current block.timestamp; the mutant inverts that choice and can set unlockTime to a past value when _unlockTime > block.timestamp.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored unlockTime is never less than the pre-call block.timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp); the mutant can set acc.unlockTime to a past value for some _unlockTime, violating this.

For any caller, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the stored unlockTime is equal to either block.timestamp or _unlockTime, and specifically it is always >= min(block.timestamp, _unlockTime); the mutant flips the choice when _unlockTime>block.timestamp and can make stored unlockTime < block.timestamp for some fuzzed _unlockTime, violating this invariant.

For any caller and any msg.value, after calling Put(_unlockTime) the caller's recorded balance increases by exactly msg.value (i.e., Acc[msg.sender].balance_post = Acc[msg.sender].balance_pre + msg.value); the mutant that subtracts msg.value after adding breaks this invariant for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount, after a successful Put call the contract's recorded Acc[msg].balance is at least as large as it was before the call (i.e., the Put never decreases the stored balance); the mutant that subtracts msg.value after adding can violate this by leaving the stored balance unchanged while previously it was smaller (thus not strictly non-decreasing) for some inputs.

For any caller and any payable amount, calling Put updates the account's unlockTime to at least the current block timestamp (i.e., acc.unlockTime >= block.timestamp after Put); the mutant still sets unlockTime but can leave stored balance unchanged in ways that allow different observable state — however the reliable universal observable invariant is that unlockTime is set to max(_unlockTime, block.timestamp), which the buggy change does not affect, so we instead assert that address(c).balance increases by msg.value (the contract's ETH balance must increase by the sent value) — the mutant subtracting msg.value from acc.balance does not alter contract balance, so this invariant still holds and distinguishes versions when combined with stored balance checks triggered by fuzzing.

For any caller and any payable amount and unlockTime, if the caller's pre-Put stored balance is zero and they send a nonzero msg.value, then after Put the contract's ETH balance increases by msg.value AND the caller's stored Acc.balance becomes equal to msg.value; the mutant that subtracts msg.value after adding can leave Acc.balance unchanged (zero) while contract balance increased, so this property fails for some inputs.

For any caller and any nonzero msg.value, if their pre-Put stored balance is strictly less than msg.value then after Put the stored Acc.balance strictly increases (becomes >= previous + 1), but the mutant that subtracts msg.value can keep the stored balance unchanged, so this invariant holds for the reference and is violated by the mutant for some fuzz input.

If an account's balance is at least MinSum and at least the requested amount, then collecting exactly when block.timestamp equals the account's unlockTime must NOT transfer funds (i.e., collection succeeds only strictly after unlockTime).

If an account's balance is at least MinSum and at least the requested amount, collecting at timestamp equal to the account's unlockTime must not allow withdrawal (collection must require block.timestamp > unlockTime).

property_summary: For any caller and any amount, if a caller has a stored balance >= MinSum and >= requested amount and block.timestamp is strictly greater than their stored unlockTime then Collect(...) succeeds and reduces contract balance accordingly; the mutant allowing >= instead of > lets collection succeed exactly at unlockTime, which the reference disallows.

For any caller/amount/unlockTime, if the caller previously deposited >= MinSum and set unlockTime equal to the current block.timestamp, then the reference contract C disallows Collect(_) at that exact timestamp (reverts or does not transfer), while the mutant allowing '>=' would permit Collect at block.timestamp == unlockTime; the test asserts that Collect called at block.timestamp == unlockTime does NOT succeed on the reference.

For any depositor who previously Put at least MinSum and set an unlockTime, calling Collect(...) at block.timestamp == unlockTime must NOT succeed on the reference (requires block.timestamp > unlockTime), but the mutant with '>=' would allow success at that exact timestamp.

For any depositor and amount, if they previously Put at least MinSum with unlockTime equal to the current block.timestamp, then calling Collect(...) at that exact timestamp must NOT succeed on the reference (it requires block.timestamp > unlockTime), whereas the mutant that uses '>=' would allow success.

For any depositor, if they previously Put at least MinSum with unlockTime equal to the current block.timestamp, then calling Collect(...) at that exact timestamp must NOT succeed on the reference (requires block.timestamp > unlockTime); the mutant changing the check to '>=' allows Collect to succeed at block.timestamp == unlockTime and thus violates this rule.
If an account's recorded balance is strictly less than c.MinSum, then calling Collect cannot transfer Ether out (no reduction of contract balance for that account).
